chunks: "Take a midday nap, for indeed the Shaytan does not take a midday nap."

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانَ: the Shaytan; the devil, mentioned here in contrast to a recommended human practice
key_terms.رُوِيَ: it is narrated; indicates a report transmitted without a stated sanad here
key_terms.فَإِنَّ: for indeed; introduces the reason or explanation
key_terms.قِيلُوا: take a midday nap; an imperative plural command to rest at midday
key_terms.يَقِيلُ: takes a midday nap; rests at midday

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about taking a midday nap (qaylulah)?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages taking the midday nap known as qaylulah. It presents this practice as a beneficial and recommended habit by contrasting it with Shaytan, who does not observe it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Take a midday nap (Qailulah), for indeed the Shaytan does not take a nap."
